question: What is the main goal of bedside teaching in midwifery?

options.B: To replace traditional classroom lectures entirely
options.C: To connect theoretical knowledge with practical patient care
options.D: To reduce the workload of senior staff nurses

explanation: Bedside teaching brings classroom concepts directly to the ward so students can see and practice real care. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why is bedside teaching different from a normal classroom lecture?

options.A: It prevents students from making any clinical mistakes
options.B: It removes the need for patient consent during tutorials
options.C: It allows students to pass exams without studying theory
options.D: It exposes learners to the authentic environment of maternity units

explanation: Real clinical settings provide practical experience with actual patients that a classroom cannot fully replicate. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is a key focus during clinical bedside teaching?

options.A: Memorizing textbook definitions without patient interaction
options.B: Managing the hospital budget and drug inventory
options.C: Developing systematic physical assessment and history-taking skills
options.D: Writing formal research papers for hospital administration

explanation: Bedside teaching focuses on hands-on clinical skills like physical exams and talking to patients. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h2)

question: How does bedside teaching help students build good communication skills?

options.A: By forcing them to memorize medical terminology in silence
options.B: By letting them practice speaking empathetically with women in pain or anxiety
options.C: By limiting their conversations strictly to written documentation
options.D: By teaching them how to lecture large groups of people

explanation: Interacting directly with real patients teaches students how to offer emotional comfort and clear explanations. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is the first thing an instructor should do with a patient before starting a bedside teaching session?

options.A: Ask her to fill out a written examination paper
options.B: Ask for clear permission to involve students in her care
options.C: Begin examining her abdomen without speaking
options.D: Move her to a private lecture hall away from the ward

explanation: Patients must always give consent before they are included in clinical teaching sessions. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why is it helpful to brief the student before meeting the patient at the bedside?

options.A: It prevents the patient from asking any questions
options.B: It eliminates the need for any supervision by the instructor
options.C: It gives the learner time to review relevant clinical knowledge and focus
options.D: It ensures the student can perform the delivery completely alone

explanation: Knowing the focus beforehand helps students pay attention to the right clinical signs during the session. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h3)

question: How should instructors and students view the patient during a bedside teaching session?

options.A: As an active participant deserving full respect and privacy
options.B: As a passive teaching object whose feelings do not matter
options.C: As a hospital employee responsible for student grades
options.D: As a public spectator watching a demonstration

explanation: Patients keep their right to privacy, dignity, and respect even when participating in teaching sessions. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which of these actions goes against patient dignity during clinical teaching?

options.A: Discussing the patient's condition across her bed as if she were not present
options.B: Drawing privacy curtains around the bed before the examination
options.C: Exposing only the specific area needed for a physical check
options.D: Asking for permission before letting a student palpate the abdomen

explanation: Talking about a patient as if she is absent strips away her dignity and ignores her presence. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h4)

question: When is clinical feedback most helpful for a student midwife?

options.A: At the end of the semester during final written exams
options.B: Months after graduation when working in a primary health centre
options.C: Immediately or very close to the time the action occurred
options.D: Only when the student makes a severe clinical error

explanation: Prompt feedback helps students connect the comments directly to what they just did. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h5)

question: A student struggles with an abdominal palpation during a bedside session. What is the best way for the instructor to handle this?

options.A: Stop teaching entirely and take over all patient care duties
options.B: Correct the technique gently while reassuring the patient and student
options.C: Scold the student loudly so other patients know standards are high
options.D: Wait until the end of the rotation weeks later to mention it

explanation: Gentle, immediate guidance protects patient confidence while helping the student learn safely. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is a common challenge when doing bedside teaching in busy Nigerian health facilities?

options.A: Too many instructors available for every single student
options.B: An excess of quiet time with no patients around
options.C: A complete absence of pregnant women in the hospital
options.D: Overcrowded wards and frequent clinical emergencies

explanation: Busy government hospitals often deal with high patient volumes and sudden emergencies that disrupt teaching plans. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h6)

question: What should an instructor do if a sudden ward emergency interrupts a teaching session?

options.A: Punish the students for being present during the emergency
options.B: Ignore the emergency so the teaching session can finish on schedule
options.C: Cancel all future clinical teaching in the hospital permanently
options.D: Pause the lesson gracefully, attend to the emergency, and resume later if possible

explanation: Patient safety and urgent care always take priority over scheduled teaching sessions. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h6)
